In Islamic tradition, Prophet Suleiman (AS) was gifted by Allah dominion over the wind, animals and Jinn, with medieval texts associating this power with his star-engraved signet ring.
Khatam means “seal”; the Quran describes Prophet Muhammad ﷺ as Khatam an-Nabiyyin - the Seal of the Prophets and final messenger. Esoteric traditions drew a conceptual connection between the Seal of Suleiman, symbolising physical and spiritual dominion, and the Prophet’s spiritual seal.
The Suleimani Star was later widely adopted across the Muslim world as a symbol of protection and blessing, appearing in Ottoman flags, coins and Islamic architecture.

caption_full:
An Inheritance of Beauty
“Log chalay jaatay hain, cheezain reh jaati hain.”
We often hear these words when a loved one passes away, usually as a reminder that there is little point in filling our lives with things we cannot take with us.
But my mother loved things. She spent a lifetime collecting them, from jewellery, shawls and saaris to antiques and curious artefacts, each chosen with an instinctive and discerning eye for beauty.
When she left, her things remained. And thank God for that because things have a way of being so unequivocally there for you. Objectively very solid behaviour from inanimate objects that got ensouled with fragments of her taste, her sensibilities, her affections and the life she lived so fully.
These things collected with love become more than possessions. They become vessels of memory, holding something of us long after we are gone, offering comfort to those left behind through something of our eternal essence.
Perhaps the true value of the things we collect is not in possessing them, but in the meaning they acquire by being chosen. Our home remains a shrine to everything Amma chose to make her own.
We may leave this world empty-handed, but the inheritance we leave behind need not be empty of us.
🌹

This 13th of Rajab, I felt called to make the Maula pendant, an inspired reproduction of my Amma’s most-worn piece of jewellery. Of everything she owned, this was the one thing that felt inseparable from her. She loved it so deeply that she had it replicated for friends and family, so it could live on beyond her, close to other hearts. 🤍
Many of you followed its making as it unfolded on my stories. My hope was simple: just as it had for Amma, I wanted this pendant to find its way into someone’s life carrying comfort, protection and guidance from the gatekeeper of divine wisdom. ✨
This Rajab also brought back a childhood memory. One evening we looked at the moon through binoculars because someone said Ali’s name was etched on it. Maybe it was in our imaginations or our faith laden lens - but that night, we saw it too. And once you witness something like that, it settles inside you. To this day, when I look at the moon, I see Ali (AS), a miracle in my everyday quietly watching over me. 🌙
And in this very month, without planning, Bibi reached 21k - a number tied to Maula’s shahadat. It felt like the same kind of silent miracle, a gentle reassurance from above. Another wondrous sign woven into my everyday, leaving me feeling seen and protected by Allah and His beloveds, just as the moon watches over the earth. 🤲🏼

There’s something incredibly beautiful about the people of Gilgit. I’ve always admired Gilgitis for their warmth, hospitality, honesty and the peaceful energy they carry. Every interaction leaves you with a feeling that’s hard to put into words — pure, genuine and beautiful.

And the way they welcome and honour their guests? Truly one of a kind. It’s not just hospitality; it’s a feeling that stays with you long after you’ve left.
And perhaps that’s what inspired me to turn this experience into something of my own. I created a handmade cuff inspired by the art, colours and soulful essence of people creations from @kadoofficial_ . A little piece of this beautiful journey, translated into my own language of art.
This cuff bracelet will forever hold a special place in my heart. A little piece of Gilgit, crafted with love and inspired by its people. ❤️
